# Cloud session listing fixtures

These files are the cloud session listings `test_adopt_original_session.py` passes with `--cloud-sessions-file`. The row shape (`id`, `title`, `session_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `environment_kind`, `status_bucket`, and the page's `has_more`, `first_id`, `last_id`) and the `{"ccr": {...}}` wrapper of a `get_session` result were recorded from the host's own `list_sessions` and `get_session` calls on 2026-10-24, trimmed to those keys: `list_page_more.json`, `list_page_complete_without.json`, `get_session_unrelated.json` (the unrelated session `session_01EayHcxxpijEm9tM6zQzVqu` is the recorded row), and the running rows of `list_page_complete_running.json` and `get_session_running.json`, whose id and title are the fixture lane's (`session_01FixtureLane0000000000`, `issue-656-fixturelane000001`) and whose `REVIEW_READY` bucket is the handed-back field case. Absence needs a newer row: a complete page proves a session gone only when its newest row was created at or after the lane started (and its rows run newest-created first), so the page spans the session's creation and a cursor-read last page cannot hide it. The seeded lane starts at 2026-10-24T12:00:00Z; `list_page_complete_without.json` (created 11:13:25Z) is therefore the older last-page case that proves nothing, and `list_page_complete_newer.json` (synthetic: the same unrelated row, created 12:30:00Z, with `environment_id` `env-1`, the seeded lane's cloud environment) is the healthy case. `list_page_complete_archived.json` and `list_page_complete_failed.json` are synthetic: no archived or failed row was observed, so they carry the recorded row shape with `session_status` set to `SESSION_STATUS_ARCHIVED` and `status_bucket` set to `SESSION_STATUS_BUCKET_FAILED`, which are the host's spelling inferred from the running values.

Two more files were recorded from the live host on 2026-10-24 (the builders' account: 100 `list_sessions` rows, 63 of them archived, 97 carrying `environment_id`, `created_at` strictly newest first), trimmed to the keys the listing reader uses. `get_session_archived_recorded.json` is a real archived session: `session_status` `SESSION_STATUS_ARCHIVED` with `status_bucket` `SESSION_STATUS_BUCKET_COMPLETED`, plus `environment_id` and `environment_kind`. `list_page_recorded_newest.json` is the newest row of a real no-cursor page, whose `has_more` was true on the real page and stays true here. The archived spelling (`SESSION_STATUS_ARCHIVED`, bucket `COMPLETED`) and `environment_id` are therefore now observed. No `FAILED` bucket has been observed yet, so `list_page_complete_failed.json` stays synthetic.
